rubric.label: Has adapted or co-produced international IP/formats
rubric.guidance: Trade-press coverage of a format deal, an adapted foreign show in credits, or co-pro credit with a non-US company. STRONGEST signal.

rubric.label: Makes content in TVF lanes (comedy, slice-of-life, young-adult, workplace)
rubric.guidance: Check credits/website/YouTube. Full points if core focus; half if occasional. LOWERED 2026-08-20 from 25 (owner rubric review): genre mismatch matters but should weigh less than proven IP-adaptation history or live distribution.

rubric.label: Live output relationship with a streamer/network/major platform
rubric.guidance: A co-pro must land somewhere. First-look deals, recent commissions, or consistent platform sales count.

rubric.label: Right size: ~2-20 core people, most under 10, real credits, independent
rubric.guidance: Lean team, not a small studio in name only. Big enough to execute, small enough to want a partner. Headcount hints plus credit history. RAISED 2026-08-20 from 15 (owner rubric review): operational fit is a harder constraint than the original weight implied.

rubric.label: Named decision-maker identified and reachable
rubric.guidance: Auto-set by the engine: 1.0 if a target-role contact has a valid email, 0.5 if catch-all, else 0.

rubric.label: Demonstrated openness to collaboration: explicit invitation, collective/partner-led model, or co-production track record
rubric.guidance: Full credit for an explicit collaboration/partnership invitation on their own site, a collective or partner-led operating structure, or a track record of co-productions. Half credit for a weaker or implicit signal. Distinct from international_ip_experience, though the two can overlap. ADDED 2026-07: default weight 15. CONFIRMED 2026-08-20 (owner rubric review): kept at 15 despite the overlap with international_ip_experience -- an explicit partnership invitation or collective structure is meaningfully different from having actually adapted a format before. Rubric pool now sums to 110 (was 115) after this review; the engine renormalizes over assessed points regardless of the pool's absolute sum, so this is a relative-weight statement, not a percentage.

score_modifiers.label: PENALTY: output dominated by client/branded-content work, not owned IP
score_modifiers.guidance: A /work page full of brand-client logos is a NEGATIVE, not a portfolio positive. 1.0 = entirely client work (full -20), 0 = no evidence of client-work dominance (no penalty). Soft subtractor, not a hard gate.

score_modifiers.label: BONUS: existing India/Asia ties, diaspora-crossover audience, or prior work with an Indian company
score_modifiers.guidance: Rare signal. Most good leads will legitimately score 0 here, which is not a strike against them. Kept small and additive so it never overrides the 5 primary fit signals.

score_modifiers.label: PENALTY: revenue estimate above the ~$1M microbudget-scale ceiling (borderline vs clean fit)
score_modifiers.guidance: Private production companies rarely publish revenue, so this cannot be verified directly. Estimate via third-party tools (e.g. LeadIQ, Buzzfile, RocketReach) where available, else reviewer judgment. 1.0 = a confirmed third-party estimate above ~$1M (borderline), 0 = at/under ~$1M or microbudget-scale (clean fit) or no negative evidence. Soft subtractor by design, matching a flag-rather-than-auto-drop preference - a reviewer can still drop borderline rows manually if being strict. RAISED 2026-08-20 from -10 to -20 (owner rubric review): now weighted as seriously as client_work_dominance. NOT YET CONNECTOR-AUTOMATED: LeadIQ/Buzzfile/RocketReach free-tier usability for this pipeline has not been adversarially verified the way every other tool in this project has been (see impl. plan §10) - until that verification happens, this input is set by the reviewer/manual lookup at S7.5, not by any connector.

gates.label: Primary operation/HQ must be in the United States
gates.guidance: Fires ONLY on confirmed non-US evidence (e.g. YouTube channel country field explicitly non-US). Blank/unknown always passes through.

gates.label: Exclude majors, their named subsidiaries, and anything clearly oversized
gates.guidance: Name/keyword match against known majors, or a confirmed size signal well beyond the ~50-person ceiling. Blank/unknown always passes through.

gates.label: Must have SOME reachable presence: website, owned channel, or social
gates.guidance: A YouTube channel itself already satisfies this for connector-sourced candidates, so this gate effectively always passes them.

gates.label: Company/channel must be currently active, not dormant or defunct
gates.guidance: Fires ONLY on confirmed dormancy (e.g. no upload or site activity in 12+ months, an explicit closed/discontinued notice). Blank/unknown always passes through. The connector makes a cheap best-effort read from upload recency at discovery time; Layer B enrichment gets a fuller look once it actually visits the site, and can override that initial guess.

youtube_discovery_queries.query: slice of life web series studio

news_rss_discovery_queries.query: "scripted format" OR "unscripted format" US remake producer

wikidata_discovery.guidance: Wikidata SPARQL seed. entity_classes: Q1762059 is film production company, Q10689397 is television production company. They are SIBLING classes, not parent/child - a live probe on 2026-08-28 showed the film tree alone misses 124 US TV production companies with websites, so both are queried via VALUES and each subclass tree is still walked. country Q30 is the United States, which is what makes geography_signal us a fact rather than a guess. A live probe on 2026-08-25 found 363 US production companies carrying an official website (P856) - and the website is the whole point: every other connector leaves domain null, and Apollo matches organisations by domain at P16. CC0, no key, no quota. Notable-only, so this is a seed re-run occasionally rather than a weekly stream, and it skews LARGE - the first page is Icon Productions, Relativity Media, Warner Independent. Expect a low hit rate against the 2-20 person target and lean on major_or_oversized_signal plus the P13 gate. Only 14 of 363 carry an employee count, so size stays an enrichment question. For Segment 2, change entity_class here rather than touching any code.

sources.name: YouTube Data API v3 (search+channels)
sources.detail: BUILD FIRST. PRIORITY: digital/YouTube/social studios. 10k units/day free. Filters creators-vs-studios by size/keyword/email-in-description; sets genre_fit from the genre_hint of the matched query, plus the 4 gate-input signals.

sources.name: Google News RSS (keyword + site: trades)
sources.detail: SIGNAL: catches deal-announcement headlines such as a US shop adapting a foreign format. Company named leads to a high international_ip_experience score.

sources.name: X/Twitter intent posts via Google News RSS
sources.detail: SIGNAL: founder-collab posts via a site:x.com Google News RSS query. Not the X API (paid-only since Feb 2026). Noisy and partial, needs a filter step plus human review.

sources.name: Wikidata SPARQL
sources.detail: Film/TV/streaming producer seed: name plus official website plus industry. CC0, free forever. Notable-only, so a seed rather than a stream.

sources.name: AICP member directory (scrape)
sources.detail: Commercial/branded shops. Static HTML, names only, needs domain enrichment downstream. ToS is reference-only.

self_exclusion.guidance: TVF and its affiliates must never enter the lead pool. This is not hypothetical: the first live YouTube run on 2026-08-24 surfaced The Viral Fever own channel among 125 candidates. It was caught only because 13.1M subscribers tripped the major_or_oversized gate - a smaller affiliate channel, a regional spinoff, or a partner shop would have sailed through, been scored, reviewed, and eventually put on a send list. Matching is deliberately conservative: domains match on exact host or subdomain, name_patterns match as whole words against a lowercased entity name. Note the absence of a bare tvf pattern - it would match TVFoods, TVFirst and similar unrelated names, and a self-exclusion rule that quietly deletes real leads is worse than the problem it solves. Add specific affiliate names here as they come up rather than broadening the patterns.

auto_shortlist.guidance: Owner decision 2026-09-21: automatically shortlist all companies with a score over 30. Every ready_for_review lead with fit_score strictly above min_score is shortlisted by the last step of the promote chain (sql/14_auto_shortlist.sql), the same rule LCX clipping has run at 20 since 2026-09-14. Leads between the review threshold (25) and 30 stay in To review for a person. Rejected, archived and contacted rows are never touched, and a lead a person moves back to review is never shortlisted again (metadata.auto_shortlisted_at). Shortlisting sends nothing: the draft it leads to still needs approval. Set enabled to false to go back to shortlisting by hand.

enrichment.guidance: Apollo is the enrichment and verification backbone (owner decision 2026-08-20): organization match by domain, then people search filtered to target_contact_roles, then Apollo verification status mapped onto contacts.email_status. Hunter (pattern oracle) and Reoon (verifier) were dropped from the critical path on the same date, and the pattern-guess hedge they required is deleted with them. The site-scrape path survives only as backlog item B1, disabled by default: it is pulled into the ladder only if Checkpoint 2 (P17) shows Apollo missing more than roughly 30 percent of 2-10-person shops. Live since 2026-09-20 (tools/enrich_apollo.py, the enrich_apollo step of the weekly refresh): open leads with a website and no address get one Apollo search on their domain, filtered to target_contact_roles, and the best person is revealed for 1 credit. enabled gates the spending and is true for this segment only -- the decision that day was production houses, not clipping or startups. credits_per_run caps a run, verified_only asks Apollo for addresses it has checked, recheck_after_days is how long a company Apollo did not know is left alone. score_over limits the spending to leads scoring above it: the owner set 30 on 2026-09-21 and lowered it to 22.5 the same day (any lead over 22.5 with no contacts: find and add them), because a company with nobody to write to is missing the 10 contact points. A written address earns the lead those points and re-scores it. find_website_by_name looks a lead without a website up in Apollo by its exact name (1 credit) and takes the website only when exactly one company carries that name and no other lead holds it.

An email goes out from the Gmail of the person who approved it, from the address of theirs with the most room today, up to that address's own limit (daily_cap on its user_mailboxes row, 35 by default; daily_send_cap here is not used in this mode). templates.subject: From TVF in India — On {{theme}}
templates.guidance: The owner's outreach template (samples of 2026-09-18). Four paragraphs: who we are and what we make; which is why this company caught our attention; the partnership and why it fits; a short call. {{angle_line}} and {{partnership}} are the owner's sentences for the company's lane, from outreach.angles. {{hook}} is "Which is why <company> caught my attention." and a paragraph about the company written from what it says about itself (generated_paragraph; the plain paragraph in tools/draft_render.py when no model writes one). {{theme}} is the subject's theme. A human reads every draft before approval. This one when the email greets a named person (samples 5 and 6). 2026-09-21, the owner: the email comes from Vedansh (the footer's sender) and is written on Kartikeya's behalf, so the opening names Kartikeya and his role while the sign-off is the footer's.

Four paragraphs: who we are and what we make; which is why this company caught our attention; the partnership and why it fits; a short call. {{angle_line}} and {{partnership}} are the owner's sentences for the company's lane, from outreach.angles. {{hook}} is "Which is why <company> caught my attention." and a paragraph about the company written from what it says about itself (generated_paragraph; the plain paragraph in tools/draft_render.py when no model writes one). {{theme}} is the subject's theme. A human reads every draft before approval. This one when no person is named (samples 1 to 4). 2026-09-21, the owner: written on Kartikeya's behalf by the footer's sender, as in the named template.

angles.guidance: The owner's own sentences for each lane a production company works in, taken from the samples of 2026-09-18. tools/draft_render.tvf_angle() picks the lane from what the company says about itself and what the engine recorded: animation, then documentary and impact work (conscience), then digital-first (digital), then scripted drama and genre (drama), else general. intro_line ends the first paragraph, partnership is the third, theme is the subject when no model writes one.

general.intro_line: Much of our work draws its strength from telling deeply local, human stories with enough craft to travel far beyond India.
general.partnership: That shared instinct is why I wanted to reach out. India is one of the world's richest and least-tapped sources of stories, talent and IP, and I believe there is real potential in how a house like {{company}} and a studio like ours might work together, whether through co-production, international financing, or developing series and films designed to cross borders from the start.

animation.intro_line: Storytelling has always been the core of what we do, and we are now extending it into animation, an area we have been building toward deliberately and are keen to grow with the right partners.
animation.partnership: Part of this is a deliberate move into kids and family content built for a global audience, drawing on Indian stories and characters with the potential to travel worldwide. I believe there is real potential in how our storytelling and your artistry might come together, whether co-developing original films and series, or building new IP that reaches audiences of every age across our markets.

conscience.intro_line: Much of our best work comes from a single instinct: giving honest, often overlooked lives the dignity of being told well, and telling them with enough craft to travel.
conscience.partnership: That shared instinct is why I wanted to reach out. India holds an extraordinary depth of underrepresented and untold stories, and very few have reached a global audience with the care they deserve. I believe there is real potential in how our two companies might work together, whether co-producing character-driven film and series, or bringing these kinds of stories across our markets.

digital.intro_line: We built long-form scripted storytelling on YouTube in India before the traditional system took us seriously, and grew from there into series, formats and film.
digital.partnership: That shared belief is why I wanted to reach out. India is one of the richest and least-tapped sources of stories, talent and IP anywhere, and I believe there is real potential in how an indie studio like {{company}} and a studio like ours might work together, whether through co-financing, co-production, or developing series designed to travel. This is precisely the kind of non-standard partnership we are built to lead.

drama.intro_line: Our work has always been built on telling deeply local, human stories with a craft that lets them travel far beyond India.
drama.partnership: That shared belief is why I wanted to reach out. India is one of the world's richest and least-tapped sources of exactly these stories, in epics, thrillers, grounded fantasy and character-driven drama, and I believe there is real potential in how a studio like ours and {{company}} might work together, whether through co-production, adaptation, or developing high-concept stories designed to cross borders from the start.

generated_paragraph.guidance: The one paragraph of the owner's template no fixed text can write: what makes this company worth writing to, and why that matches how TVF thinks. Written by a model from tools/draft_render.tvf_facts(): what the company says about itself on its own site (title, description, about page), its named work, its founders, a dated headline about it, and its lane; nothing else, and nothing about TVF, which the model otherwise borrowed to describe the company. Every name, title, place and number it writes must be in those facts, and so must every quoted phrase; no TVF claims, links, sales or flattery words, nothing about co-production or financing (the next paragraph says that); no relative dates ("this December", "recently"); the company named at most once; 15 to 75 words, short rather than padded when the facts say little; genre words found on the site are left out of what the model sees (one "humorous" became a documentary studio that weaves in comedy); the subject theme may not name anyone. A rejected answer gets one retry, told why. Anything still failing, a lead with nothing of its own on record (a page title alone is not enough), or no GROQ_API_KEY: the plain paragraph (draft_render.tvf_fit_fallback). Three requests a minute keeps inside the free plan's 8,000 tokens a minute. The paragraph is stored on the outreach row, so what a person approved is what is sent. See tools/llm.py.

outreach.guidance: Everything outbound is drafted -> human-approved -> sent, in that order, no exceptions. daily_send_cap is a hard ceiling per send run. One outbound touch per company is enforced by the database (uq_outreach_one_touch), not by this config. The footer -- sign-off, postal address, opt-out -- is one setting for the whole segment (outreach.footer.text), edited in the app under Outreach -> Footer; templates end with {{footer}}.

footer.guidance: The owner's sign-off (2026-09-18): Warm regards, then the sender's name and title -- Kartikeya until 2026-09-21, when the owner set Vedansh Gupta, Outreach Consultant, who writes on Kartikeya's behalf (the templates' opening says so). Under it, the postal address and the one-line way out that commercial email must carry and the footer check requires. Edited in the app: Outreach -> Footer. It may use {{sender_name}}, {{sender_title}} and {{postal_address}}. Templates end with {{footer}}; see tools/draft_render.py.
